newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas mostly ends up on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas mostly ends up on warmer weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Thursday in lackluster trade, with front months buoyed most of the day by forecasts for warmer Midwest and East Coast weather next week and a steady cash.
August firmed 1.7 cents to close at $2.115 per million British thermal units. September settled 0.7 cent higher at $2.124. Most other months ended with slim gains.

"The cash held because we're going to get some heat again later this week and next. Until the cash breaks down, I think you'll see the board (futures) hold," said a Midwest trader, adding he expected modest gains near-term on the weather.
While some said growing inventories will eventually weigh on the market, most agreed there was little conviction about market direction and little reason for prices to move far from current levels.

Revised forecasts are calling for warmer Midwest and East Coast weather later this week and early next week, but seasonal to below-seasonal weather is expected later. Heat is forecast to continue in Texas and the West for the period.

Chart traders agreed the market was range bound. They pegged August support at this week's $2.051 low, with psychological buying likely at $2. Resistance was seen first at $2.15, with major selling expected along the down trendline now in the $2.24 area.
In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices eased slightly to the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to one cent lower in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was little changed in the high-$2.30s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose one-half cent to $2.202. NYMEX said 23,566 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 29,507.

On the KCBT, August finished 1.5 cents higher at $2.005, while deferreds ended down by 0.3 to 0.5 cent. The East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 11.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 107 lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 100.
